test_title: SSC MTS (2022) Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: According to census 2011, what is the population (nearest value) of tribals in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**10.42 crore.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **According to the 2011 census, the population of tribals in India is 10.42 crore. (hence option 1 is correct)**
 
• This constitutes 8.6% of the country's total population.
 
• The top 5 states with the largest tribal population are:
 
 
• Madhya Pradesh
 
• Maharashtra
 
• Odisha
 
• Jharkhand
 
• Chhattisgarh
 
 
 
• These 5 states together account for over 60% of the total tribal population in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Census 2011:

 
• Census 2011 was the 15th National Census of India conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India under the Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India.
 
• The census was conducted in two phases: the first phase was conducted in April 2010 and covered the states of Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Kerala, Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland, Punjab, Rajasthan, Sikkim, Tamil Nadu, Tripura, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, and West Bengal, along with the Union Territories of Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, Lakshadweep, Delhi, and Puducherry.
 
• The second phase was conducted in February-March 2011 and covered the remaining states and Union Territories.
 
• The main objective of Census 2011 was to provide comprehensive and reliable data on population characteristics, such as size, distribution, and socio-economic and demographic characteristics.
 
• The census collected information on various parameters, such as age, sex, literacy, education, occupation, migration, religion, and housing.
 
• The data collected during the census is used for planning and policy-making purposes by the government and other stakeholders.
